name: Dominica
summary: An Indigenous stronghold gradually drawn into the colonial contest.
notes: French settlers arrived before formal administration in 1727. The Kalinago people maintained communities through colonization and remain part of Dominica today.

events.title: Spain claims Dominica
events.detail: Columbus sighted the island on a Sunday; no Spanish colony followed.
events.qualification: A European claim; it does not establish island-wide administration or extinguish Indigenous rights.

events.title: A French claim
events.detail: French claims preceded organized settlement and rule.
events.qualification: A European claim; it does not establish island-wide administration or extinguish Indigenous rights.

events.title: Dominica reserved for the Kalinago
events.detail: An agreement between Indigenous representatives, France and England recognized Indigenous possession.

events.title: French settlement expands
events.detail: French settlers arrived among Kalinago communities.
events.uncertainty: An approximate marker for a gradual process, not a dated island-wide handover.

events.title: French administration established
events.detail: Organized French government followed the earlier settlements.

events.title: Neutrality on paper
events.detail: Britain and France declared neutrality while French settlers remained.

events.title: Britain captures Dominica
events.detail: A Seven Years’ War expedition took the colony.

events.title: British sovereignty confirmed
events.detail: The Treaty of Paris assigned Dominica to Britain.

events.title: French forces retake Dominica
events.detail: France captured the island during the American Revolutionary War.

events.title: British government restored
events.detail: The 1783 peace settlement returned the colony.

events.title: The Commonwealth of Dominica independent
events.detail: The associated state became an independent republic.
